Resolves #21620

🌿 A planner in Tokyo no longer has to ask what the Berlin rota means on their own clock.

Related: #21346 · #21140 · #21613

Adds `examples/scheduler/timeZones`: a follow-the-sun support rota for the weekend of 31 October, nine agents in Tokyo, Berlin and New York, with every shift stored in UTC. A segmented switch, one named group for assistive technology, sets the time axis to the viewer's own zone, Berlin, New York or Tokyo. The zone and the range go into one `timeAxis.set()`, so the range's day keys resolve on the new clock: the hours and day boundaries keep their place on screen, and every shift moves to its time in that city. Each day's header names the city and its offset; a day whose clocks change says which way and by how much. On Sunday 1 November New York leaves daylight time, so in New York time that day has 25 hours, `01:00` comes twice, and the header reads `clocks go back 1 h: UTC−4 → UTC−5`. Each bar names its agent's hours on their own clock (`07:00–15:00 in Tokyo`); the readout under the toolbar lists the chosen shift on every clock of the team and the viewer, the agent's own and the axis' clock lit, then its stored UTC times. No engine change, no shared file.

Evidence: L3 (Chromium at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, five themes, the browser pinned to Los Angeles; `TimeZones.spec.mjs` in `e2e-engine`; the frames and cold read below) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-7 are rendered layout, zone switching and look). Residual: none for #21620; publication belongs to #21613.

`agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline PR baseline + guards ran`

## Deltas from ticket

- The weekend of 31 October 2026 puts a clock change inside the plan: New York's on Sunday at 02:00, and Los Angeles's too for a West Coast viewer. Every agent works the same local hours on both days, so New York's Sunday shifts are stored one hour later than its Saturday ones. The axis spans Friday to Monday in every zone, so no shift falls off it in any city.
- Switching the zone re-anchors the axis on Friday midnight of the chosen city. The day boundaries keep their place on screen, and the shifts move past them. That is the ticket's "every shift moves and the day boundary moves with it", read from the shifts.
- A click or Enter on a bar chooses the shift for the readout, and the timeline column's `highlightedRecordIds` marks it.
- At full width the plan opens at Saturday 15:00, so Sunday's clock change is the next thing on screen. Below 720px it shows ten hours labelled by their number, the zone switch is a two-by-two grid, and the plan opens at the chosen shift and follows it across zones.
- The drive found no engine defect that blocks this ticket. It found one behaviour worth a look, filed as a defect-note: `timeAxis.set({timeZone})` alone keeps bare-key `start` and `end` as instants, so day ticks fall at another hour in the new zone, while bare `nonWorkingDates` keep their civil dates. The example passes the range in the same `set()`, which is correct usage today.

Red controls: with the range dropped from the zone's `set()`, the first two tests fail at this head: Haruto Sato's Sunday bar lands at 1,755 px instead of 2,475 px in Tokyo time, and New York's Sunday reads only `UTC−5`, because its tick then starts at 03:00 New York time. The `group` assertion failed against the first head, whose `vdom` override never reached the DOM; the switch now takes `role: 'group'` and its label through `changeVdomRootKey`.

Frame critique: at 1440 about 160 px stay empty below the nine rows (accepted: nine rows of 64 px fill a laptop screen, and taller rows would only fatten the bars). A bar that starts before the view truncates its label (`12:00–20:…`); the label stays sticky inside the visible part, so the rest reads once it scrolls in (accepted). The chosen shift's mark is a lighter border, which is quiet on the amber bars (accepted: the readout names the shift and lights its clocks).

## Cold look

One reader of this seat (Claude Sonnet, no session context) read this head's four frames beside `scheduler/basic`'s: **desktop 7/10, phone 5/10** (`scheduler/basic`: 6 and 4); better than the sibling at both sizes, "a story (follow-the-sun staircase, per-zone readout)" on desktop and controls that reflow on a phone. (The first head's reader went with the session that ran it; its findings are the revision in `f9a412cade`.) Findings and their fate:

| Finding | Fate |
|---|---|
| Phone: the Tokyo rows open empty, no cue their shifts lie left | accepted: the phone opens at the chosen shift and the readout lists every clock; a zone switch brings each city's shifts in |
| Phone: the day header is cut mid-sentence; stub bars read `…` | accepted: a pinned label at 390 px; bar labels stay sticky inside their visible part |
| Switching the clock changes which shifts are in view | intended: the axis keeps its clock time, so the shifts move (the ticket's look-for) |
| `01:00` appears twice with no marker | accepted: Sunday's header says `clocks go back 1 h`; marking the hour row would be a header change in the engine |
| A bar says `07:00–15:00 in Tokyo` yet sits at 15:00–23:00 | intended: a bar keeps its agent's clock, the axis the chosen one; the hint says so |
| Edge labels cut (`18:0`), 160 px below the last row, small muted text | accepted (critique above) |
